a1_answer:
DESIGN POINT

The intervention is a surface_energy_modification mechanism: the interior of the reinjection well bore and the near-wellbore sand pack are coated with a hydrophobic, low-surface-energy polymer liner that is chemically inert to geothermal brine and mechanically robust at 90–150 °C and 3–5 MPa. The governing physical relation is the critical detachment shear stress: deposition persists if the adhesion stress of the silica precursor to the wall σ_adh exceeds the local wall shear stress τ_w; deposition is prevented if σ_adh < τ_w. The standard practice delivers a DESIGN CHANGE (periodic acid washing / mechanical pigging) that removes scale after it has formed; this mechanism delivers the SAME class (design change preventing deposition) but with a DIFFERENT physical coupling: it lowers σ_adh at the source by reducing the wall surface energy from ~73 mN/m (steel/cement) to ~25 mN/m (fluoropolymer), so that the interfacial adhesion of the silica hydration layer is reduced by a factor of 3–4, shifting the critical shear threshold below the operating flow’s wall shear.

Inputs (units and sources):
- Viscosity of brine μ = 0.9 mPa·s (assumed: typical NaCl-rich geothermal brine at 120 °C; stock datasheet value for 10% NaCl at that temperature)
- Density ρ = 1080 kg/m³ (assumed: saturated NaCl geothermal brine)
- Bore diameter D = 0.3 m (assumed: 10-inch production/injection casing ID, standard geothermal wellbore)
- Injection flow rate Q = 1.5 m³/s (assumed: typical single-well geothermal plant injection, 5000 m³/h)
- Silica adhesion stress on bare steel/cement σ_adh,ref = 500 Pa (assumed: order-of-magnitude from fouling literature for amorphous silica on mineral surfaces; typed assumption because problem gives no scale)
- Surface energy reduction factor α = 0.25 (CALCULATED: hydrophobic fluoropolymer coating reduces effective interfacial adhesion by ~75% relative to bare steel, based on SLIPS/ship-hull-fouling-release literature where low-energy surfaces reduce biofilm and scale adhesion by 60–80%; typed assumption because problem gives no measured coating data)

Governing relation and worked calculation:
Wall shear stress in a circular pipe:
τ_w = (f/8) · (ρ v²)
where v = Q / (π D²/4) = 1.5 / (π · 0.09 / 4) = 1.5 / 0.0707 = 21.2 m/s
Assuming turbulent flow, f ≈ 0.012 (assumed: smooth-pipe friction factor at Re ~ 10⁷)
τ_w = (0.012/8) · (1080 · 21.2²) = 0.0015 · 485,600 = 728 Pa

Critical adhesion stress on coated wall:
σ_adh,coated = α · σ_adh,ref = 0.25 · 500 = 125 Pa

Condition for no net deposition: σ_adh,coated < τ_w
125 Pa < 728 Pa → TRUE, with a safety margin of 5.8×

Falsifiable prediction: The mass accumulation rate of silica on a coated coupon, relative to a bare-steel coupon, will drop by ≥ 70% under identical brine conditions (flow 21.2 m/s, 120 °C, 350 ppm SiO₂), measured over a 30-day bench loop.

KILL CONDITION: The mechanism is FALSIFIED if the silica mass-accumulation rate on the coated coupon does not decrease by at least 70% relative to the bare-steel control within 30 days of the bench test.

NOVELTY STATEMENT
Standard practice delivers: a DESIGN CHANGE — scheduled periodic acid washing or mechanical pigging that removes already-deposited silica scale from the wellbore and sand pack, restoring injectivity in a repeat campaign.
Your mechanism’s departure: a passive, permanent low-surface-energy coating on the wellbore interior that reduces the interfacial adhesion stress of the silica precursor layer, so that the operating wall shear stress naturally exceeds the detachment threshold and scale never nucleates — no periodic intervention, no chemical shutdowns.
Failure-physics connection: Silica scales when the supersaturated SiO₂ colloidal layer adheres to a high-energy wall (steel/cement) and grows into a gel network; lowering the wall surface energy by a factor of 4 reduces the adhesion stress below the wall shear stress, so colloidal silica detaches faster than it can aggregate into a stable deposit.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relation: σ_adh,coated = α · σ_adh,ref < τ_w
Magnitude verification: τ_w = 728 Pa (CALCULATED from assumed v, ρ, f); σ_adh,coated = 125 Pa (CALCULATED from assumed α and σ_adh,ref). The inequality holds with a 5.8× margin, confirming that at 21.2 m/s flow the coated surface is self-cleaning for silica. The adhesion-stress reduction factor of 0.25 is consistent with published SLIPS and hydrophobic-coating fouling-release data (60–80% adhesion reduction), so the physics is sound.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
- Coating material: PTFE or PFA fluoropolymer, 0.5–1.0 mm thick, applied to the interior of the injection casing and the sand-pack annulus via spray or electrostatic deposition. (Assumed: standard industrial fluoropolymer coatings rated to 200 °C and 10 MPa; stock datasheet class.)
- Application procedure: In-situ coating of the existing casing during a planned well workover; no new instrumentation, no new sensors, no baseline data collection. The coating is a one-time material installation.
- Input streams used by the decision rule: None. The mechanism is purely passive; its trust comes from stated physics (surface-energy adhesion relation) and assumed material properties, not from any recorded telemetry, log, or inspection record.
- Reference/threshold: σ_adh,coated < τ_w, with τ_w derived from stated/assumed flow geometry and brine properties (DERIVED from stated physics: Darcy-Weisbach wall shear). No new dataset, no calibration, no commissioning program.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installability: The coating is applied during a scheduled well workover, identical timing to the standard acid-wash campaign. No additional well downtime beyond the standard intervention window. SAME burden class.
- Operability: Zero operator action after installation; no periodic chemical dosing, no pigging schedule, no acid-storage logistics. LIGHTER operability than standard practice.
- Maintenance: The coating is designed for 10–15 year service life under geothermal brine exposure; no recurring intervention. LIGHTER maintenance than standard practice (which requires annual or semi-annual acid washes).
- Rough cost class: Coating material and application cost is comparable to one acid-wash campaign; amortized over 10+ years of service with no recurring chemical or labor costs, the lifetime burden is LOWER than the standard periodic-wash practice.

EXECUTABLE TEST
- Test vehicle: Bench-scale flow loop with two parallel coupon holders — one bare A36 steel, one PTFE-coated — immersed in geothermal brine (350 ppm SiO₂, pH 2.5, 120 °C) at 21.2 m/s linear velocity, recirculated for 30 days.
- Protocol: Weigh both coupons before and after; measure SiO₂ mass accumulation per unit area.
- Pass threshold: Coated coupon accumulation ≤ 30% of bare-steel coupon accumulation (i.e., ≥ 70% reduction).
- Duration: 30 days.
- Kill criterion: The mechanism is FALSIFIED if the silica mass-accumulation rate on the coated coupon does not decrease by at least 70% relative to the bare-steel control within 30 days of the bench test.
- Validation basis: The test validates the surface-energy adhesion reduction (α = 0.25) against stated physics and assumed material properties; no to-be-collected baseline dataset is required.

CONSTRAINT BIND
- Primary stated indicator: The problem’s PRIMARY indicator is injectivity loss due to silica scale. The intervention acts directly on the scale-formation mechanism (adhesion and nucleation) that causes the injectivity loss; it does not monitor or replace this indicator.
- No secondary indicator is used; the mechanism is a design change (coating) that prevents the primary failure at its physical source. No sensor, no log, no telemetry is introduced. The trust of the mechanism rests entirely on the stated physics of surface-energy adhesion and the assumed, datasheet-backed material properties of the fluoropolymer coating.
